title_original: ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back His Cretinous Fake OG Talk-Show Host, Only Now Ali G Is the Film’s ‘Political’ Subject. A Mistake, Innit?
editorial_title_zh: 《Ali G：我是谁？》（Ali G: Who Iz I?）评测：萨莎·拜伦·科恩带回了他那个愚蠢的假 OG 脱口秀主持人，只是现在的 Ali G 成了电影的“政治”主题。这不是搞砸了吗？
editorial_excerpt_zh: 通过将 Ali G 变成他自己的荒诞传奇中的笨蛋反英雄，《我是谁？》（Who Iz I?）基本上变成了萨莎·拜伦·科恩版本的《周六夜现场》（Saturday Night Live）电影，就像《马格鲁贝尔》（MacGruber）、《斯图尔特拯救全家》（Stuart Saves His Family）或《洛克斯堡之夜》（A Night at the Roxbury）一样。这部电影有一些零星的搞笑时刻，但是……

and Butt-Head）的方式被叫停。）但这一切都太少、太迟了。如果《Ali G：我是谁？》的意图是像《波拉特》对2000年代的美国那样去揭露和讽刺今天的美国，那么这部电影基本上没有击中靶心。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但这不是它的意图。萨莎·拜伦·科恩在采访中以及在《时代》杂志的高调封面文章中曾表示，他想要带回 "interviews", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/sacha-baron-cohen-ali-g-problematic-joke-1236917651/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "片中还引入了 Ali G 的死对头，一位名叫尼拉·凯恩-恩德格切洛博士（Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degeocello）的教授，同样由拜伦·科恩饰演，他埋在乳胶假体和服装之下，变成了一个七十岁左右的左翼嬉皮老人（秃顶的发顶和马尾辫、傲慢的牛蛙般下垂的脸颊、细边眼镜、花纹毛衣），声音尖锐而又满口狂热的高论。他是电影对“觉醒文化”（wokeness）的恶搞。《我是谁？》既嘲笑 Ali G，也嘲笑那个不惜一切代价要让他闭嘴的书呆子对手。这部电影正试图在毒性极端的时代里，成为一场面向所有人的无差别扫射式闹剧。正如 Ali 自己所说：“我被‘取消’了（cancelized）。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但问题就在这里。通过将 Ali G 是白人，教授需要一个 DNA 样本，而他获取样本的那段戏迎合了粗俗的看客群体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "身无分文的 Ali G 和 Julie 抵达了洛杉矶，因为 Ali 以为自己可以复活曾在 HBO 播出了2季的脱口秀系列。（该节目于2004年结束。）当事实证明他无法复活时，他落入了一个右翼电视网的手中，对方愿意让他主持“言语自由秀”（The Free Speech Show）。其中包含了法西斯式的闲聊和埃隆·马斯克式的直臂敬礼。萨莎·拜伦·科恩还饰演了埃兰·莫拉德上校（Col. Erran Morad），这位前摩萨德特工带有浓厚的以色列口音（他是这三个角色中最不好笑的一个）。莫拉德带头绑架了 Julie，后者在一个充满疯狂造假感的场景中产子，民兵队员们则客串起了产科医生。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "即便是在我身为 Ali G 粉丝的日子里，当我视他为一个令人愉悦的笨蛋时，他最搞笑的时候也是作为脱口秀的丑角，去愚弄那些不幸坐下来接受他采访的名流官员。并不是说我想了解他的背景故事，或是看他走过场般地演一出虚假的救援惊悚片。但《Ali G: Who Iz I?》却偏要塞进这些内容，因为这部电影忙于证明其存在的合理性，以至于犯了一个错误，假装 Ali G“至关重要”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "《Ali G: Who Iz I?》影评：萨莎·拜伦·科恩带回了他那个白痴般的虚假 OG 脱口秀主持人，只是现在 Ali G 成为了电影的“政治”主题。这可真是个错误，对吧？", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "于2026年10月20日在纽约 AMC 林肯广场（AMC Lincoln Square）进行审看。美国电影协会（MPA）评级：R。片长：89分钟。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "出品：Amazon MGM Studios 发行，Four by Two Films、Working Title Films 联合出品。制片人：萨莎·拜伦·科恩（Sacha Baron Cohen）、彼得·杰基（Petr Jáki）。执行制片人：蒂姆·贝万（Tim Bevan）、埃里克·费尔纳（Eric Fellner）、丹·马泽（Dan Mazer）、彼得·贝恩汉姆（Peter Baynham）、安东尼·海恩斯（Anthony Hines）、萨曼莎·豪斯曼（Samantha Housman）、阿拉·凯希尚（Ara Keshishian）、莫妮卡·莱文森（Monica Levinson）、斯图尔特·米勒（Stuart Miller）、路易斯·罗斯纳（Louise Rosner）、亚历克西斯·桑皮耶特罗（Alexis Sampietro）、斯黛西·谢尔（Stacey Sher）、戴尔·斯特恩（Dale Stern）、丹·斯威默（Dan Swimer）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "演职员：导演：萨莎·拜伦·科恩（Sacha Baron Cohen）。编剧：萨莎·拜伦·科恩（Sacha Baron Cohen）、安东尼·海恩斯（Anthony Hines）、彼得·贝恩汉姆（Peter Baynham）、丹·斯威默（Dan Swimer）、丹·马泽（Dan Mazer）、基莎·佐拉（Keisha Zollar）。摄影：克里斯·达内尔（Chris Darnell）、卢克·盖斯布勒（Luke Geissbuhler）、马库斯·门茨尔（Markus Mentzer）。剪辑：克雷格·阿尔珀特（Craig Alpert）、马克·戴维斯（Mark Davies）、迈克尔·贾姆布拉（Michael Giambra）、黛布拉·尼尔-费舍尔（Debra Neil-Fisher）。音乐：埃兰·拜伦·科恩（Erran Baron Cohen）、娜米·梅卢马德（Nami Melumad）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "演员：萨莎·拜伦·科恩（Sacha Baron Cohen）、莫加娜·罗宾逊（Morgana Robinson）、斯图尔特·罗德海弗（Stewart Rodeheaver）。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Back in the day (as he would have put it), Ali G was my favorite Sacha Baron Cohen character. In the ’90s and early 2000s, there was something exquisitely daft about his track suit and do-rag wave cap, his “street” Cockney Jafaican patois, his insanely stunted worldview and brain-dead malapropisms (“Does you think that men should marry only one woman? Does you believe in mahogany?” ), and in the more than slightly absurd Method commitment with which Baron Cohen immersed himself in the character.", "links": [{"text": "Sacha Baron Cohen", "url": "https://variety.com/t/sacha-baron-cohen/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Screenshot-2026-10-23-at-3.55.05-PM-e1792785333330.png?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "Hila Klein, Ethan Klein", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Ethan Klein Reacts to Hila Klein's Cheating Allegations Amid 'H3 Podcast' Fallout: 'Please Respect My Family's Privacy ... They Have Nothing to Do With This'", "links": [{"text": "Ethan Klein Reacts to Hila Klein's Cheating Allegations Amid 'H3 Podcast' Fallout: 'Please Respect My Family's Privacy ... They Have Nothing to Do With This'", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/digital/news/ethan-klein-reacts-hila-klein-cheating-allegations-h3-1236929836/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ethan-klein-hila-klein.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "Hila Klein and Ethan Klein", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair", "links": [{"text": "H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/digital/news/hila-ethan-klein-affair-h3-podcast-cuts-ties-1236925732/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "That said, Ali G would never have been more than an inspired sketch-comedy jape if it hadn’t been for all the politicians and public figures he interviewed — a parade of po-faced luminaries (Donald Trump, Ralph Nader, Buzz Aldrin, Christie Todd Whitman, Sam Donaldson), none of whom had any idea that they were being punked by a walking put-on. I’ll never forget the look on Pat Buchanan’s face when Ali G asked him if the U.S. had found “BLTs” in Iraq."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But that was then. The joke of Ali G is that he was a maximally clueless white-bro poseur (a ripely legitimate topic for satire, since millions of white kids in Britain and the U.S. had mindlessly appropriated the style and attitude and language of hip-hop culture). But it’s a joke of its era that sits uncomfortably in the world of today. In 2026, the character of Ali G is so out of step that his presence now risks playing as an ironic nostalgic celebration of something it once skewered."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“ Ali G: Who Iz I? ” is a movie that would like to do for Ali G what “Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan” (2006) did for Borat and “Bruno” (2009) did for Bruno. Except that the new movie, which Baron Cohen directed himself, isn’t like those other films. They were guerrilla comedies, more documentary than not (pundits have been drawing comparison between “You Can See Everything” and “Borat”), in which the bulk of the comedy consisted of Borat or Bruno talking to ordinary Americans, who didn’t know they were being pranked, in a way that unmasked their idiocies and prejudices.", "links": [{"text": "Ali G: Who Iz I?", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ali-g-who-iz-i/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There’s some of that in “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” but it’s all fairly minor and neutral. When Ali G’s romantic partner, Julie (Morgana Robinson), who’s pregnant with their child, attempts to purchase a mansion in Bel Air, the real-estate agent is the “straight” character (i.e., he’s not in on the joke), but he’s treated with total dignity. He’s just there to shuttle increasingly extreme messages back and forth between Ali G and Julie in what becomes a glorified comedy routine."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There’s a scene with a liquor-store salesman who, likewise, isn’t the butt of the joke. And there are several scenes in which Baron Cohen, in character, talks to groups of people sitting in rows in meeting rooms — and what he says is so appalling that they walk out, or simply turn on him. These vérité extras aren’t there so that the film can ridicule or belittle them; they come off just fine. At the climax, a handful of right-wing would-be militia men are used as the butt of the joke in an elaborate sequence that’s all about foiling terrorists. (It’s also arrested in a “Jackass”/”Beavis and Butt-Head” way.) But it’s too little, too late. If the intent of “Ali G: Who Iz I?” is to reveal and skewer America today, as “Borat” did to the America of the 2000s, the film mostly misses its mark."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But that’s not its intent. Sacha Baron Cohen has stated, in interviews and in a lofty cover essay in Time magazine, that the real reason he wanted to bring Ali G back is precisely because the character is now so dated and “problematic.” Between innocuous guerrilla bits, “Who Iz I?” really is about Ali G. He shows up in his bling, with his dreds tucked under a rastacap, and the movie proceeds to deconstruct what a relic he is (he has a testy back and forth with a DEI counselor), goofing on his attitudes even as it’s milking them for cheap laughs.", "links": [{"text": "interviews", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/sacha-baron-cohen-ali-g-problematic-joke-1236917651/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "It also introduces Ali G’s foil, a professor named Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, also played by Baron Cohen, buried under latex prosthetics and a costume that turns him into a seventyish left-wing boomer (balding pate and ponytail, arrogant bullfrog jowls, wire-framed glasses, patterned sweaters), with a whiny voice of voracious high-mindedness. He’s the film’s parody of “wokeness.” “Who Iz I?” mocks Ali G, and it also mocks the geek adversary who will do anything to shut him down. The movie is trying to be an equal-opportunity drive-by farce for the age of toxic extremes. At one point, as Ali puts it, “Me was cancelized.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But here’s the problem. By turning Ali G into the doofus antihero of his own absurdist saga, “Who Iz I?” becomes Sacha Baron Cohen’s version of a “Saturday Night Live” movie, like “MacGruber” or “Stuart Saves His Family” or “A Night at the Roxbury.” The film has a few scattered giggles, but it’s dawdling and cumbersome, and far less “relevant” than it thinks. For a brief spell, Ali falls under the delusion that he’s the biological son of A$AP Rocky, and this makes for comedy that’s both intentionally and unintentionally cringe. To prove that Ali is white, the professor needs a DNA sample, and the sequence in which he gets it plays to the yahoo peanut gallery."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ali G and Julie, flat broke, have arrived in L.A. because Ali thinks he can revive his talk-show series that ran for two seasons on HBO. (It ended in 2004.) When it turns out that he can’t, he falls into the grip of a right-wing network that’s willing to feature him as the host of “The Free Speech Show.” There’s fascist banter and Elon Musk stiff-arm salutes. Baron Cohen also plays Col. Erran Morad, the former Mossad agent who speaks in a thick Israeli accent (he’s the least funny of the three characters). Morad spearheads the kidnapping of Julie, who gives birth in a scene of gonzo fakery, with the militia men acting as obstetricians."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Even in my days of Ali G fanhood, when I found him to be a delectable idiot, he was most funny as a talk-show stooge, punking the famous functionaries who had the misfortune to sit down and be interviewed by him. It’s not as if I wanted to know his backstory or watch him go through the motions of an ersatz rescue thriller. But “Ali G: Who Iz I?” lays on that stuff, because the film is so busy working to justify its existence that it makes the mistake of pretending that Ali G “matters.”"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back His Cretinous Fake OG Talk-Show Host, Only Now Ali G Is the Film’s ‘Political’ Subject. article_text:
Back in the day (as he would have put it), Ali G was my favorite Sacha Baron Cohen character. In the ’90s and early 2000s, there was something exquisitely daft about his track suit and do-rag wave cap, his “street” Cockney Jafaican patois, his insanely stunted worldview and brain-dead malapropisms (“Does you think that men should marry only one woman? Does you believe in mahogany?” ), and in the more than slightly absurd Method commitment with which Baron Cohen immersed himself in the character.

Related Stories

Ethan Klein Reacts to Hila Klein's Cheating Allegations Amid 'H3 Podcast' Fallout: 'Please Respect My Family's Privacy ... They Have Nothing to Do With This'

H3 Podcast Crew Cuts Ties With Ethan Klein After Hila Klein Says He Has Been Having an Affair

That said, Ali G would never have been more than an inspired sketch-comedy jape if it hadn’t been for all the politicians and public figures he interviewed — a parade of po-faced luminaries (Donald Trump, Ralph Nader, Buzz Aldrin, Christie Todd Whitman, Sam Donaldson), none of whom had any idea that they were being punked by a walking put-on. I’ll never forget the look on Pat Buchanan’s face when Ali G asked him if the U.S. had found “BLTs” in Iraq.

But that was then. The joke of Ali G is that he was a maximally clueless white-bro poseur (a ripely legitimate topic for satire, since millions of white kids in Britain and the U.S. had mindlessly appropriated the style and attitude and language of hip-hop culture). But it’s a joke of its era that sits uncomfortably in the world of today. In 2026, the character of Ali G is so out of step that his presence now risks playing as an ironic nostalgic celebration of something it once skewered.

“ Ali G: Who Iz I? ” is a movie that would like to do for Ali G what “Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan” (2006) did for Borat and “Bruno” (2009) did for Bruno. Except that the new movie, which Baron Cohen directed himself, isn’t like those other films. They were guerrilla comedies, more documentary than not (pundits have been drawing comparison between “You Can See Everything” and “Borat”), in which the bulk of the comedy consisted of Borat or Bruno talking to ordinary Americans, who didn’t know they were being pranked, in a way that unmasked their idiocies and prejudices.

There’s some of that in “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” but it’s all fairly minor and neutral. When Ali G’s romantic partner, Julie (Morgana Robinson), who’s pregnant with their child, attempts to purchase a mansion in Bel Air, the real-estate agent is the “straight” character (i.e., he’s not in on the joke), but he’s treated with total dignity. He’s just there to shuttle increasingly extreme messages back and forth between Ali G and Julie in what becomes a glorified comedy routine.

There’s a scene with a liquor-store salesman who, likewise, isn’t the butt of the joke. And there are several scenes in which Baron Cohen, in character, talks to groups of people sitting in rows in meeting rooms — and what he says is so appalling that they walk out, or simply turn on him. These vérité extras aren’t there so that the film can ridicule or belittle them; they come off just fine. At the climax, a handful of right-wing would-be militia men are used as the butt of the joke in an elaborate sequence that’s all about foiling terrorists. (It’s also arrested in a “Jackass”/”Beavis and Butt-Head” way.) But it’s too little, too late. If the intent of “Ali G: Who Iz I?” is to reveal and skewer America today, as “Borat” did to the America of the 2000s, the film mostly misses its mark.

But that’s not its intent. Sacha Baron Cohen has stated, in interviews and in a lofty cover essay in Time magazine, that the real reason he wanted to bring Ali G back is precisely because the character is now so dated and “problematic.” Between innocuous guerrilla bits, “Who Iz I?” really is about Ali G. He shows up in his bling, with his dreds tucked under a rastacap, and the movie proceeds to deconstruct what a relic he is (he has a testy back and forth with a DEI counselor), goofing on his attitudes even as it’s milking them for cheap laughs.

It also introduces Ali G’s foil, a professor named Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, also played by Baron Cohen, buried under latex prosthetics and a costume that turns him into a seventyish left-wing boomer (balding pate and ponytail, arrogant bullfrog jowls, wire-framed glasses, patterned sweaters), with a whiny voice of voracious high-mindedness. He’s the film’s parody of “wokeness.” “Who Iz I?” mocks Ali G, and it also mocks the geek adversary who will do anything to shut him down. The movie is trying to be an equal-opportunity drive-by farce for the age of toxic extremes. At one point, as Ali puts it, “Me was cancelized.”

But here’s the problem. By turning Ali G into the doofus antihero of his own absurdist saga, “Who Iz I?” becomes Sacha Baron Cohen’s version of a “Saturday Night Live” movie, like “MacGruber” or “Stuart Saves His Family” or “A Night at the Roxbury.” The film has a few scattered giggles, but it’s dawdling and cumbersome, and far less “relevant” than it thinks. For a brief spell, Ali falls under the delusion that he’s the biological son of A$AP Rocky, and this makes for comedy that’s both intentionally and unintentionally cringe. To prove that Ali is white, the professor needs a DNA sample, and the sequence in which he gets it plays to the yahoo peanut gallery.

Ali G and Julie, flat broke, have arrived in L.A. because Ali thinks he can revive his talk-show series that ran for two seasons on HBO. (It ended in 2004.) When it turns out that he can’t, he falls into the grip of a right-wing network that’s willing to feature him as the host of “The Free Speech Show.” There’s fascist banter and Elon Musk stiff-arm salutes. Baron Cohen also plays Col. Erran Morad, the former Mossad agent who speaks in a thick Israeli accent (he’s the least funny of the three characters). Morad spearheads the kidnapping of Julie, who gives birth in a scene of gonzo fakery, with the militia men acting as obstetricians.

Even in my days of Ali G fanhood, when I found him to be a delectable idiot, he was most funny as a talk-show stooge, punking the famous functionaries who had the misfortune to sit down and be interviewed by him. It’s not as if I wanted to know his backstory or watch him go through the motions of an ersatz rescue thriller. But “Ali G: Who Iz I?” lays on that stuff, because the film is so busy working to justify its existence that it makes the mistake of pretending that Ali G “matters.”

‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Brings Back His Cretinous Fake OG Talk-Show Host, Only Now Ali G Is the Film’s ‘Political’ Subject. A Mistake, Innit?

article_text:
Daidō Moriyama: Ink ★★★★☆

If it’s a crime to have a crush on an elderly avant garde Japanese street photographer then lock me up and throw away the key, because I have some seriously strong feelings for Daidō Moriyama . His ultra-confrontational, high contrast, aggressive take on photography just gets me blushing, what can I say.

This little exhibition is Moriyama at his artiest and strangest. In the 1960s he discovered Warhol and became obsessed. The works here find him playing with repetition and silk screening, printing up ghostly, painterly, effervescent monochrome images of stacks of soft drinks, neon lit crosswalks and peep show adverts. This is the grim, gritty side of Japanese urbanity, but you can see American capitalism creeping in and taking hold, slowly suffocating the streets.

He repeats an image of lips like Warhol’s Marilyn Monroe, duplicates a photo of people walking down a street, their bodies becoming indistinguishable from the adverts hanging from the high rises around them. Then he snaps a woman lifting her skirt, another stomping down the road in thigh-high boots. It’s like Warhol without the pretence, and with added filth. Hamiltons Gallery, London, until 14 November

Jenkin van Zyl: Enclosure ★★★★☆

Jenkin van Zyl is hellbent on cementing their place as English art’s ultimate hyper-camp weirdo, and their new show at Somerset House Studios is a pretty persuasive argument.

The exhibition is centred on a speculative sci-fi movie about some bleak company where tourists can inhabit other people’s bodies. But when the central character, a starlet called Mercy, comes to end the lease on her body, the line between reality and fiction starts getting anxiously blurry. Who is the real Mercy, and who is the clone? Who controls your identity? Who has access to what makes you you ?

Its grubby atmosphere is reinforced by an immersive installation that replicates the film set as you walk in, with broken automatons, flickering lights and piles of rubbish, all bathed in a pink glow. It’s an unsettling, uncomfortable, dirty, dystopian bit of art cinema – like an overblown, fetishistic take on Terry Gilliam’s Brazil . Van Zyl has a singular aesthetic, and this is pretty much as watchable as this kind of art film gets. It stays with you long after you’ve escaped its unnerving clutches.

The gallery handout wants to make out like this is about technological advancement and ideas of authorship. But like all good sci-fi, this feels more obviously allegorical than that. It’s about identity, the versions of ourselves that we present and preserve online, or in public, and how easy it is to lose your grip on the true you. Like a lot of artists these days who grew up with the internet and reality TV turning their brain into gloop, Van Zyl is trying to make sense of a post-reality world, a place where identity can be constructed, but never fully controlled. Somerset House, London, until 29 November

George Shaw: Albion Groans Part Two ★★★★☆

There’s nothing all that pleasant, or even particularly green, about the England of George Shaw’s paintings. There are no rolling hills or quiet pub afternoons here in this excellent show of small works by the 60-year-old artist. Instead, there are endless potholes, crumbling masonry, darkened alleys and damp, muddy, miserable, mid-winter landscapes. This is the England of council estates left to rot.

His landscapes – always based on his native Coventry – are devoid of life. There are no humans here, only the places they’re desperate to escape. Every sky is overcast, every tree barren, every path sodden with puddles. A union jack has been left crumpled on the pavement near an empty bottle of booze in one, endless knobs have been crudely graffitied on garage doors in another. There’s a painting of a single cloud blighting a blue sky, another of a robin lying dead on its side. Suburbia has leached into the countryside like a toxic spill.

They are gorgeously painted, especially the smaller works: sticky with enamel, glossy and horrifyingly alluring, like staring at a car crash.

But the car crash here is England itself. Sure, Shaw has been painting the same views of the same bit of Coventry for 30 years, but in that time the country has continued to erode. His whole career is a living portrait of England’s slow collapse. This time it doesn’t just feel like perpetual decline – it’s terminal. Anthony Wilkinson Gallery, London, until 7 November

after newsletter promotion

Tanoa Sasraku: Tropical Ken ★★★☆☆

The thing that’s so good about the main work in Tanoa Sasraku’s Turner prize installation – open now at Mima in Middlesbrough – is how perfectly it marries image with idea. Sasraku’s collection of corporate paperweights from oil companies acts as a horrifying symbol of the greed of that vile industry. Perfect.

Here at Vardaxoglou, Sasraku is showing works from another series, some of which are also on show at Mima, that don’t quite hit the same dopamine receptors. They’re all paper cut into the form of torsos, held together with clips. She places acetates of military camouflage on top of them and then pops them in a tanning bed, leaving behind the faintest impressions of the patterns.

They’re meant to evoke warfare, weapons crates and fruit boxes, all while alluding to Ken dolls, but they just look a bit like tea-stained gilets. The gap between image and idea, between the concept and its ability to communicate itself visually, is just a bit too wide. Vardaxoglou, London, until 31 October

editorial_excerpt_zh: 庞贝考古公园的发掘调查显示，在被公元79年维苏威火山喷发掩埋的一处住宅中，发现了木制储物柜的痕迹。其中存放着童年护身符、化妆工具以及青铜硬币等，揭示了当时日常生活的一角。Ark […]

article_text:
ポンペイ「青の間」顔料代は、ローマ兵年収の最大9割!? 最新調査結果が発表｜2024年にポンペイで発見された「青の間」の最新調査により、壁を覆う顔料の使用量と価値が明らかになった。その費用はローマ兵の年収の最大約9割に相当するとされ、当時の富裕層による豪奢な装飾の実態が浮かび上がった。【続きを読む】 Photo: Facebook/Archaeological Park of Pompeii

ポンペイ考古学公園で2024年に発見された「青の間」。Photo: Facebook/Archaeological Park of Pompeii

ポンペイの家族を襲った悲劇が明らかに。ドアをベッドで封鎖し最期まで抵抗を試みる｜考古学者たちがポンペイ遺跡にある「ヘレとフリクソスの家」を調査したところ、子ども1人を含む4人の遺骨が見つかった。調査を進めたところ、突然の災害から最期の瞬間まで生き延びようとした家族の物語が明らかになった。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy Pompeii Archaeological Park

「ヘレとフリクソスの家」の食堂。Photo: Facebook/Pompeii Archaeological Park

「ヘレとフリクソスの家」の食堂。Photo: Facebook/Pompeii Archaeological Park

「ヘレとフリクソスの家」の室内。Photo: Facebook/Pompeii Archaeological Park

「ヘレとフリクソスの家」の寝室で見つかった木製ベッドの石膏型。Photo: Facebook/Pompeii Archaeological Park

CTスキャンでポンペイ「逃亡者の庭」の犠牲者の職業が判明──携えていたのは「医療箱」｜西暦79年のヴェスヴィオ火山噴火の惨状を今に伝えるポンペイの遺跡「逃亡者の庭」。そこに残された14人の犠牲者のうち、うずくまった男性の職業が最新研究によって明らかになった。【続きを読む】Photo: Ivan Romano/Getty Images

ポンペイ近郊「ポッパエアの別荘」で鮮やかなフレスコ画を発見。孔雀や仮面の精細な描写が姿を現す｜ポンペイに近いトッレ・アヌンツィアータで発掘が進む遺跡で、ポッパエア・サビナの別荘からポンペイ第2様式のフレスコ画が新たに見つかった。ポッパエアは、古代ローマ帝国第5代皇帝・ネロの2番目の妻。【続きを読む】 ポッパエアの別荘で発見された孔雀のフレスコ画（部分）。Courtesy of the Archaeological Park of Pompeii

古代都市ポンペイはどのように消え、いつ発見されたのか。「時が止まった」遺跡の謎を解く｜ヴェスヴィオ火山の火砕流に飲み込まれ、一瞬にして灰の中に消えたポンペイ。古代の時間が閉じ込められたこの遺跡は、今も人々の好奇心を刺激してやまない。近年も次々と新事実が明らかになるポンペイの基礎知識をまとめた。【続きを読む】Photo: LightRocket via Getty Image

ポンペイ遺跡の一区画「貞淑な恋人たちの島」に現存するフレスコ画が、新たな発見と発掘作業を経て一般に初公開された。LightRocket via Getty Images

ポンペイ遺跡にある古代ローマの円形劇場。KONTROLAB/LightRocket via Getty

ポンペイの犠牲者は、なぜ真夏に毛織物を着ていたのか──「死の文化」研究チームの最新調査が示す謎｜西暦79年8月25日に起きたとされるヴェスヴィオ山の噴火。スペインの研究チームによる最新調査で、ポンペイの犠牲者たちは、真夏には不釣り合いとも思える毛織物を身にまとっていた事実が浮かび上がった。【続きを読む】 Photo: University of Valencia

スペイン・バレンシア大学の研究チームによるポンペイ犠牲者の調査風景。Photo: University of Valencia

ポンペイに12メートルの塔があった!? 最新デジタル調査で「失われた街」の真実の姿が明らかに｜ポンペイ考古学公園は、新たなデジタル研究によって、有名な邸宅「Casa del Tiaso（ティアソスの家）」が12メートルにおよぶ塔を備えた多層建築物であった可能性が高いことが分かったと発表した。【続きを読む】 ティアソスの家の3Dデジタルモデル。Photo: Courtesy Pompeii Reset

ポンペイの食堂跡からエジプト由来の陶器を発見。古代の文化交流を明かす重要な手がかりに｜ポンペイの食堂跡から、約2000年前に作られた陶器が発見された。エジプト・アレクサンドリアで作られたとされるこの器が庶民が利用する食堂で見つかったことで、当時の文化交流の実態が浮かび上がる。【続きを読む】 Photo: Courtesy Archeological Park of Pompeii

ポンペイで1世紀ぶりに「デュオニソスの秘儀」の絵を発見｜古代ローマの都市ポンペイの遺跡で、宴会場として使用されていた部屋の3つの壁面にまたがる巨大なフレスコ画が発見された。「デュオニソスの秘儀」を描いたと考えられ、西暦79年に発生したヴェスヴィオ火山噴火の100年以上前のものと推測されている。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy of the Pompeii Archaeological Park

古代ローマ以前の巨大な墓地を北イタリアで発見｜イタリアの山岳地帯にあるトレントのサンタ・クローチェで、200基の墓がある大規模な埋葬地が発掘された。発見された副葬品から、埋葬地を造った人々が当時のイタリア半島における他の集団から文化的な影響を受けていたか、交流があったとをみられる。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy of the Press Office of the Provincial Council of Trento

炭化した巻物に「愚か」や「生命」などの文字が。AIによる古代文書の開封に進展｜X線画像とAI技術を用い、炭化した古代ローマ文書を解読する試みが新たな進展を見せた。ヘルクラネウムの巻物と呼ばれる文書の「バーチャル開封」と判読に取り組んでいるのは、ヴェスヴィオ・チャレンジの参加者だ。【続きを読む】Photo: Courtesy the Vesuvius Challenge

イタリアのナポリ国立図書館が所蔵するヘルクラネウム・パピルス（2019年撮影）。Photo: Antonio Masiello/Getty Images

火山噴火の悲惨さを物語る足跡をポンペイ近くの工事現場で発見｜イタリア・カンパニア州でメタンガス用パイプラインの改修工事を行っていた際に、ヴェスヴィオ火山噴火の悲惨さが伺える人の足跡や、古代末期に作られたとされる墓跡が発見された。これらの遺跡は、青銅器時代から古代末期までさかのぼるという。【続きを読む】Photo: Soprintendenza Archeologia Belle Arti e Paesaggio di Salerno e Avellino

Estrenos Netflix – 2 al 8 de noviembre 2026

Por: Staff Cine PREMIERE

¿Qué verás este mes?

Conoce aquí todos los estrenos de películas y también series nuevas que llegan a Netflix en noviembre de 2026. Los estrenos de esta semana están destacados en amarillo. Cada mes, la plataforma de Netflix presenta nuevos títulos de películas, series y, por supuesto, de documentales y especiales. Así pues, conoce aquí los estrenos que hay de nuevas películas y también de series de Netflix.

¿Cuánto cuesta Netflix al mes?

Netflix ofrece varios planes para que elijas el más adecuado para ti. Consulta AQUÍ los beneficios y restricciones de cada uno.

Estándar con anuncios: $119 pesos al mes

Estándar: $249 pesos al mes (más posibilidad de agregar miembros extra por $69 pesos cada uno)

Premium: $329 pesos al mes (más posibilidad de agregar miembros extra por $69 pesos cada uno)

También te podría interesar los estrenos de:

Estrenos de series en Netflix (noviembre 2026)

Los altruistas (The Altruists) (19/11/2026)

Bass X Machina (03/11/2026) ESTRENO ESTA SEMANA EN NETFLIX Serie animada para adultos creada por LeSean Thomas (Yasuke), con animación del Studio Mir (The Legend of Korra). Reimagina la historia del legendario alguacil afroamericano Bass Reeves en un Viejo Oeste retrofuturista —parte steampunk, parte pesadilla sobrenatural— donde un padre pierde el brazo en la guerra y lo reemplaza con una extremidad cibernética. Con las voces de Brian Tyree Henry y Janelle Monáe, quien también compone la música de la serie.

Palomas Negras: Temporada 2 (Black Doves) (05/11/2026) ESTRENO ESTA SEMANA EN NETFLIX Mientras Helen se adapta al rol de esposa del primer ministro y Sam recibe un ultimátum, un ataque contra Reed los lleva a buscar respuestas de forma desesperada.

Al norte del norte: Temporada 2 (North of North) (05/11/2026) ESTRENO ESTA SEMANA EN NETFLIX Renovada y lista para su próxima etapa, Siaja se apoya en la comunidad de Ice Cove para llevar su vida al siguiente nivel y construir su propio futuro.

Palacio (06/11/2026) ESTRENO ESTA SEMANA EN NETFLIX Coproducción colombiana ambiciosa producida por Dynamo ( Cien años de soledad ), resultado de más de siete años de investigación. En noviembre de 1985, un comando del M-19 toma el Palacio de Justicia de Bogotá, manteniendo como rehenes a más de 300 personas, incluidos magistrados de la Corte Suprema. La serie recorre la toma, la devastadora retoma militar y las décadas de búsqueda de justicia de las familias de las víctimas. Los tres primeros episodios son dirigidos por el guatemalteco Jayro Bustamante ( Temblores , La Llorona ). Se estrena el día exacto del aniversario 41 de los hechos.

El cuerpo (The Body) (11/11/2026) Serie creada y dirigida por Quinn Shephard ( Not Okay ). Las integrantes de un equipo de baile de un colegio católico combinan su vida religiosa con fiestas y rivalidades adolescentes. Cuando organizan una ceremonia de iniciación para una nueva compañera, un ritual que sale endemoniadamente mal las arroja a una espiral de culpa, deseos impíos y visiones que nadie sabe cómo explicar. Con Sofia Wylie y Shirley Chen.

El claroscuro (ChiaroScuro) (11/11/2026) Serie italiana. En la Galleria Nazionale di Roma aparece el cuerpo del director del museo, dispuesto como el cadáver en un famoso cuadro de Artemisia Gentileschi. El inspector Angelo Tiberi y el consultor de arte Cosmo Speranza investigan un crimen que mezcla el mundo del arte con un pasado que Cosmo creía enterrado.

La ley de Alicia (12/11/2026) Cuando su vida perfecta se derrumba, Alicia vuelve a ejercer derecho y descubre que reconstruir su carrera también significa redefinirse a sí misma.

La emperatriz: Temporada 3 (The Empress) (12/11/2026) Tanto su matrimonio como el imperio enfrentan dificultades. Isabel elige un camino que cambiará su vida ―y el futuro de Europa― para siempre.

La ley de las bestias (The Law of Beasts) (18/11/2026) Cuando un infanticida condenado está a punto de ser liberado, el pánico regresa a Polonia. La investigadora principal del caso y la psiquiatra que lo evaluó se enfrentan en un tenso duelo moral sobre la culpa, la redención y los límites de la justicia.

Gordon (18/11/2026) El director Pablo Trapero (El Clan, Carancho) y Pablo Fendrik llevan a la pantalla la historia real de Aníbal Gordon, un delincuente común que, sin abandonar sus crímenes, se convirtió en uno de los agentes parapoliciales más temidos de la Triple A en la Argentina de los años 70. article_text:
In occasione dell’edizione 2026 di Artissima , che aprirà al pubblico dal 30 ottobre al 1° novembre, Untitled Association vi accompagna alla scoperta di mostre, eventi e iniziative da non perdere nei giorni della Torino Art Week , con itinerari pensati per professionisti del settore, appassionati d’arte o semplici curiosi, tra musei, spazi istituzionali, gallerie private e spazi indipendenti.

Oggi si riparte in Borgo Filadelfia, a due passi dalla fermata metropolitana Lingotto e la sede espositiva di Artissima 2026, ancora con la Pinacoteca Agnelli . Proseguiamo in zona Crocetta con la Fondazione BuonoLopera e le OGR Officine Grandi Riparazioni ; attraversiamo poi il centro cittadino per raggiungere Vanchiglia, con una tappa al MAO – Museo d’Arte Orientale e alla galleria CRAG Gallery . Concludiamo la nostra giornata in zona Barriera di Milano con la galleria Galleria Franco Noero .

Torino Art Week 2026: gli appuntamenti di oggi

Si parte in Borgo Filadelfia, vicinissimo alla stazione della metropolitana Lingotto e la sede espositiva di Artissima 2026, con la prima tappa della giornata: la Pinacoteca Agnelli . Nell’ambito di Artissima 2026, per la nuova stagione della Pista 500, lo spazio presenta l’inedito progetto Vehicles di Iris Touliatou – vincitrice del Premio Pista 500 nel 2025 – a cura di Nicola Trezzi . La pratica artistica di Iris Touliatou esplora i limiti delle strutture spaziali, finanziarie o amministrative che governano le istituzioni che la invitano a creare, produrre e presentare il suo lavoro, siano esse musei, gallerie o biennali. Invitata dalla Pinacoteca Agnelli a creare una nuova immagine per il billboard sulla Pista 500, Touliatou realizza un progetto che va oltre il perimetro fisico dell’immagine, operando simultaneamente su molteplici livelli intrecciati tra loro. Richiamando la funzione originaria del billboard, Touliatou ha ideato una campagna di comunicazione per un corso di lingua degli uccelli come score per un’azione futura. Presentata con un pitch e affidata in outsourcing a Evergreen Design House – l’agenzia incaricata dalla Pinacoteca Agnelli di produrre i propri contenuti multimediali – la campagna viene diffusa sia sul billboard che tramite video trasmessi sopra le biglietterie dell’istituzione e sulla sua pagina Instagram. Con questo progetto poliedrico, Touliatou unisce critica istituzionale a un approccio metalinguistico per esaminare le dinamiche e i rapporti tra cose viventi e non viventi, offrendo una comprensione più profonda dell’idea di produzione e delle sue implicazioni.

Poco distante svetta, sul Grattacielo della Regione Piemonte, la Luce d’artista Swarms (Sciami) di Chiara Camoni , un intervento site specific realizzato al 43esimo piano del grattacielo. L’opera nasce dal desiderio dell’artista di introdurre, nella rigida verticalità dell’edificio, elementi inattesi: luci da discoteca e oggetti scenografici come sfere a specchi che, muovendosi e cambiando colore, creano sciami luminosi, ruotando e danzando tutta la notte «al ritmo di una musica che non si sente».

Spostiamoci in zona Crocetta, a due passi dal Politecnico di Torino per raggiungere le prossime tappe: la Fondazione BuonoLopera e le OGR Officine Grandi Riparazioni .

Sulla sommità del Politecnico di Torino, affacciata su Corso Duca degli Abruzzi, è stata presentata la luce d’artista Star*(life) di Tony Oursler , prima installazione pubblica permanente nel Paese di uno degli artisti che hanno rivoluzionato il linguaggio della proiezione e della luce, ridefinendo le possibilità espressive nello spazio pubblico e architettonico. Personaggi onirici e grotteschi dell’artista, proiettati in dimensioni monumentali, popolano le facciate della sede del Politecnico, muovendosi con ironia attraverso le galassie e i pianeti, oltre i consueti concetti di spazio e di tempo. Tony Oursler è uno dei pionieri della videoproiezione immersiva, spesso declinata in contesti ambientali e architettonici o applicata a elementi scultorei e tridimensionali. L’intervento fa parte delle quattro nuove installazioni luminose introdotte nell’ambito della 29ª edizione di Luci d’Artista.

Proseguiamo la nostra giornata con la Fondazione BuonoLopera e la collettiva Avanzi di un mondo di sogno. Su invito di Fondazione BuonoLopera, Almanac cura negli spazi di Villa Chiuminatto una mostra che riunisce le opere di tre artistɜ coinvoltɜ: Benni Bosetto , Davide La Montagna e Martina Laruffa . Il progetto invita a perdersi tra frammenti di narrazioni e immagini che costruiscono realtà e illusioni, desideri e conoscenza. A partire da corpo, memorie e affetti, le opere di Bosetto, La Montagna e Laruffa esplorano diversi modi di conoscere e interpretare il mondo, facendo emergere residui e tracce che compongono le nostre esistenze.

Poco distante le OGR Officine Grandi Riparazioni ospitano la personale Infinity mirrored room – The Eternally Infinite Light of the Universe Illuminating the Quest for Truth di Yayoi Kusama , una delle artiste più celebri e influenti del panorama artistico internazionale, recentemente scomparsa il 14 agosto 2026. Per oltre cinquant’anni Yayoi Kusama ha realizzato ambienti immersivi capaci di avvolgere completamente i visitatori e condurli all’interno del suo universo visivo. Attraverso luce, riflessi e ripetizioni, l’installazione trasforma lo spazio in un’esperienza percettiva sospesa tra meraviglia e spaesamento: punti luminosi e superfici specchianti generano l’illusione di uno spazio dalla dimensione infinita, in continua espansione. La ripetizione ossessiva di forme e pattern, elemento distintivo della ricerca dell’artista, diventa uno strumento per esplorare il concetto di dissoluzione del sé, self-obliteration, superando i confini tra individuo e ambiente e aprendo a una percezione dilatata di spazio e universo.

In mostra alle OGR anche le celebri Infinity Mirror Room, presentate nell’ambito di The Quantum Effect , a cura di Daniel Birnbaum e Jacqui Davies , il progetto espositivo dedicato alle connessioni tra teoria quantistica, cultura visiva contemporanea e nuovi modi di percepire e interpretare la realtà. The Quantum Effect , con una nuova configurazione site-specific concepita per Binario 1, riunisce opere di alcune delle figure più significative del panorama artistico internazionale, tra cui Cerith Wyn Evans , Isa Genzken , Tom á s Saraceno , Mark Leckey , Rirkrit Tiravanija , Sturtevant e Man Ray .

Attraversiamo il centro cittadino, superando Il Mastio della Cittadella, per raggiungere il MAO – Museo d’Arte Orientale e la personale Song Dong. Soul Out a cura di Li Zhenhua e Davide Quadrio , con Francesca Filisetti e Rebecca Ricci . La mostra, concepita come un progetto site-specific, coinvolge l’intero museo trasformandolo in un dispositivo narrativo in cui le opere di Song Dong entrano in dialogo con la collezione permanente e l’architettura storica di Palazzo Mazzonis. Riunendo alcune delle installazioni più note dell’artista, insieme a un archivio di fotografie e video di performance che vanno dagli anni ’90 a oggi, Song Dong. Soul Out ripercorre oltre trent’anni di lavoro mettendo in luce una pratica che intreccia esperienza individuale e storia collettiva, memoria privata e trasformazione sociale, offrendo al contempo uno sguardo sulla Cina contemporanea.

Prende avvio oggi la nuova edizione di Evolving Soundscapes , il public programme a cura di Chiara Lee e freddie Murphy che riunisce artisti della scena del suono sperimentale e della performance, con prospettive asiatiche e diasporiche. L’edizione 2026/2027 si sviluppa in dialogo con la mostra di Song Dong, con il suono che diventa uno spazio in cui la transitorietà prende forma: trasformazioni urbane, memorie intergenerazionali e reinvenzioni della tradizione vengono attraversate e rielaborate da pratiche che si muovono tra astrazione ed esperienza vissuta, percezione interiore e ambiente circostante, dimensione individuale e collettiva. Il programma, che presenta oggi alle 18 al MAO Beijing Opera Yabi , una performance di KaKa, uscirà anche dal Museo, rinnovando le collaborazioni con COMBO e OGR Torino.

Da non perdere al museo anche la collettiva Contemporary Expressions #4 di Gala Porras-Kim , Elif Uras , Dayanita Singh , Sissel Tolaas e Driant Zeneli . Con la sua quarta edizione, Contemporary Expressions , delinea la restituzione del programma di residenze artistiche e commissioni site-specific capaci di mettere in dialogo l’arte contemporanea con la collezione e gli spazi del MAO, reinterpretando il passato attraverso le prospettive e il linguaggio del presente. Installazioni site-specific, ceramiche, fotografie, video, ricerche scientifiche e olfattive rimodellano e, al contempo, destabilizzano la collezione e lo stesso Palazzo Mazzonis, che si trasforma in un imperdibile ricettacolo di interventi narrativi.

Prosegue il ciclo di appuntamenti la mostra Paesaggi da sogno / Dreamscapes di Utagawa Hiroshige a cura di Laura Vigo , dedicata alla celebre serie Le 53 stazioni della Tō kaid ō di Hiroshige, uno dei capolavori assoluti dell’arte giapponese dell’Ottocento. Come ultima tappa al museo vi segnaliamo anche Made in China la nuova installazione della galleria dedicata alla Cina, curata da Laura Vigo con la collaborazione del designer Brian Yue , il direttore del MAO Davide Quadrio e con il contributo delle artiste Sissel Tolaas e Gala Porras-Kim . Il nuovo allestimento reinterpreta la collezione archeologica cinese attraverso oltre 140 oggetti, risalenti al periodo compreso tra il Neolitico e la dinastia Tang. Ceramiche, bronzi, oggetti funerari e vetri vengono messi in relazione con le persone, le azioni, i rituali e le esperienze sensoriali che ne hanno accompagnato la creazione e l’utilizzo.

Intorno al MAO, una serie di interventi luminosi accendono il Quadrilatero della città piemontese. Via Sant’Agostino è animata dalla Luce d’artista Migrazione (climate change) di Piero Gilardi composta da dodici sagome di pellicani che, seguendo un algoritmo messo a punto dall’artista con il videomaker Heinrich Vogel , si illuminano e si spengono una dopo l’altra, alternando i colori blu, viola, rosso e giallo che rimandano al tramonto.

Alle spalle del MAO, in Piazza Palazzo di Città, troviamo invece la Luce d’Artista, il Tappeto Volante di Daniel Buren , un intervento composto da 1536 lanterne cubiche di plexiglas, parzialmente colorate di rosso o blu alternati al bianco, nelle strisce di 8,7 centimetri che caratterizzano tutte le opere di Buren, a prescindere dalla grandezza e dal luogo per cui vengono concepite. In alcune edizioni passate di Luci d’Artista, Tappeto volante era stata allestita altrove nel centro cittadino e in occasione delle Olimpiadi invernali di Torino 2006 è stata modificata sostituendo il verde al blu per celebrare i colori della bandiera italiana.

Da non perdere inoltre in Galleria Umberto I, la Luce d’artista, L’energia che unisce si espande nel blu di Marco Gastini . L’intervento si configura come una grande pittura luminosa nel tono prevalente del blu, a cui Gastini attribuiva una speciale energia, evocando “il blu di Klein, o quello di Giotto”.

Proseguiamo il nostro percorso attraversando la Dora Riparia, per raggiungere gli spazi della galleria CRAG Gallery . Per il terzo anno consecutivo, in occasione della Turin Art Week, la galleria torinese presenta DOMA , un progetto espositivo che giunge alla sua terza edizione nel 2026 con DOMA #3 – Selected Artworks . La mostra riunisce una selezione di opere di artisti italiani e internazionali, creando un dialogo tra diversi linguaggi artistici, sensibilità e pratiche contemporanee. DOMA #3 presenta opere di Adam Ka š par , Alessandro Cardinale , Bea Sarrias , Chiara Ferrando , Dominik M á lek , Alessandro Fabbris , Giacomo Modolo , Lo Chan Peng , Luca Coser , Ohsumi Hideo , Roger Coll e Sebastiano Pallavisini . La selezione riunisce diversi interventi, dalla pittura, alla fotografia e alla scultura, offrendo una panoramica multiforme delle pratiche artistiche rappresentate. Nelle sue tre edizioni, DOMA è diventato parte integrante dell’impegno costante del CRAG nel promuovere il dialogo tra artisti, pubblico e spazi espositivi, offrendo l’opportunità di scoprire la ricerca artistica contemporanea in un contesto intimo e informale. Torneremo domani a parlare della mostra presentata nella sede principale della galleria. Vi ricordiamo, inoltre, per stasera, in occasione della Notte delle Arti Contemporanee di TAG – Torino Art Galleries, l’apertura straordinaria delle due sedi della galleria dalle ore 18 alle ore 23.

CRAG Gallery cura inoltre la personale Vertiges della fotografa Chiara Ferrando , presso il prestigioso hotel NH Collection Torino Piazza Carlina. Le opere allestite sulle pareti della scala aulica sviluppano un linguaggio visivo incentrato sull’ambiguità spaziale e sulla bellezza: le forme architettoniche sono riconfigurate in composizioni dinamiche in cui lo sguardo diventa instabile e lo spettatore è immerso in uno spazio vertiginoso.

Eccoci arrivati, oltrepassato il Cimitero Monumentale presso la nostra ultima tappa: la Galleria Franco Noero e la personale Luna di Pier Paolo Calzolari . Figura centrale dell’arte contemporanea, Pier Paolo Calzolari ha sviluppato fin dagli anni Sessanta una pratica radicale e riconoscibile, capace di mettere in discussione le convenzioni della pittura e della scultura attraverso l’impiego di materiali organici e inorganici, elementi naturali e processi di trasformazione. La mostra, che riunisce principalmente opere inedite dell’artista, si inserisce nel percorso di una ricerca capace di interrogare la pittura, i suoi strumenti e le sue possibilità espressive, attraverso un linguaggio al di là dei confini tradizionali.

Per un appuntamento fuori porta vi segnaliamo la collettiva Atelier dei Moderni a cura di Sylvie Ramond presso la Venaria Reale . La mostra propone un affascinante viaggio attraverso la pittura del Novecento, esplorando l’evoluzione dell’arte moderna europea. Attraverso una selezione di opere di maestri assoluti come Henri Matisse , Pablo Picasso , Georges Braque , Andr é Derain , Jean Dubuffet , Wifredo Lam , Simon Hanta ï , Francis Bacon e molti altri, il percorso espositivo mette in luce le profonde trasformazioni del linguaggio artistico del secolo scorso: dalla ricerca della purezza delle forme e del colore fino alle tensioni drammatiche dell’Espressionismo e dell’arte figurativa postbellica.

Prima di lasciarci, vi diamo appuntamento questa sera alle 18:30 su Lungo Dora Napoli, sempre nel quartiere Aurora, da Spelonca Project per la performance Narrazione di immagini di Lina Pallotta e Bunny Dakota . La fotografa per la prima volta rovescerà la camera: presentando una narrazione di immagini dal suo archivio di vita, con uno sguardo fluido e inedite plasticità, accompagnata dal live di Bunny Dakota.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 《静止影像》（Still Image）是都灵皇家博物馆（Musei Reali di Torino）举办的展览，好莱坞明星杰西卡·兰格（Jessica Lange）在其中展现了她摄影探索中私密而精致的一面。文章《Jessica Lange：从《美国恐怖故事》片场到其摄影的私密世界。都灵展览》…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在展览发布会期间，低调内敛的杰西卡·兰格选择将发言权交给出场机构代表以及策展人安妮·莫林（Anne Morin），直到最后，只有当公众亲自向她提问时，她才拿起话筒。因此，让我们忘掉那些电影中充满爆发力的女演员，忘掉《美国恐怖故事》剧集中坚强冷艳的女性，转而走进一位精致且带点羞涩优雅的摄影艺术家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/06_Jessica-Lange-1920x1257-1024x670.jpg", "alt": "jessica lange ", "caption": "Jessica Lange, New York © Jessica Lange, Courtesy Howard Greenberg Gallery, NY", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "令人惊讶的是，在这样一个成就斐然、名声大噪并走过无数红毯的职业生涯巅峰期，杰西卡·兰格在私下里却始终将自己视作摄影师，尽管全世界都认得她并视她为演员。然而，这一特质与她的作品所传达的信息完美契合，在她的作品中，美感与魅力恰恰蕴含在每一次快门那戏剧般私密且个人的本质之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "从61号公路到荒凉的美国乡村。展览精选", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《STILL IMAGE. 杰西卡·兰格摄影展》（STILL IMAGE. Fotografie di Jessica Lange）正在都灵皇家博物馆的基亚布雷塞展厅（Sale Chiablese dei Musei Reali di Torino）展出，展期至2027年2月7日。本次展览由200多张影像组成，记录了兰格自19世纪90年代以来在旅途中遇到的风景、地点和人物。展览划分为多个主题板块；其中最值得一提的是以“61号公路”（Highway 61）命名的系列，这条公路从北到南纵贯美国，起于作者的出生地明尼苏达州，一路延伸至爵士乐之都新奥尔良——顺便提醒影迷朋友们，这也是《美国恐怖故事》第三季《女巫集会》（Coven）的拍摄地！展览路线上的另一个有趣节点，同样呼应了兰格作为演员的身份，是一组名为《畸形秀》（Freak Show）的收藏，这些照片正是在该电视剧拍摄期间创作的，在其中不难认出该系列剧集中的其他熟悉面孔。这些展出的影像带有某种忧郁色彩，充分吸收了叙事中令人痛苦的氛围，但它们似乎又扎根于一段遥远且充满悲伤困扰的时光中。", "links": [{"text": "Musei Reali di Torino", "url": "https://museireali.cultura.gov.it/"}], Courtesy Howard Greenberg Gallery, NY", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在我们个人评选的展览最佳板块中，压轴的是《往昔的存在》（Presence of the Past）系列，该系列汇集了兰格在美国乡村腹地拍摄的多幅照片。那里点缀着饱受灾难或遗弃、经济危机及人口外流摧残的地方，这些事件让整个小镇湮没在遗忘之中。用马克·奥热（Marc Augé）的话来说，这是一场非地方（non-luoghi）的巡礼，是往往围绕着后来关闭的大型工业区兴起的临界空间，作者在其中辨认出人们及其故事流连的苍白痕迹。“人们在一个地方层层叠加的手势、习惯和故事，是我拿起相机按动快门的原因，”兰格充满激情地说道，提醒我们依然存在着一个被遗忘且破败的美国，在那里动物的尸体在路边腐烂，曾经住满居民的房屋和全面投产的繁荣工厂不复存在，只留下了曾经穿行于此而后消散的人性记忆。", "许多人最初可能会因为作者的知名度而被这场新展览吸引，她在社交媒体和八卦小报上被奉为风格与标志性的女王。然而，我们倾向于认为，跨过这第一道门槛后，公众的脑海中可能会浮现出第二层体验。这层体验是通过一位女性被施展魔法般的个人视角缓缓展开的——她受过摄影师的训练，随后却走上了其他道路，她将莱卡相机作为感知和诠释世界的媒介，作为讲述并传达感受与反思的工具。影像之美存在于诸多方面：构图与主体、裁剪与执行质量、印制技术以及透视结构。", "话虽如此，杰西卡·兰格向公众呈现的并不是那种放诸四海皆完美、带有强烈作者风格、轻易可归入某种规范或标准的摄影作品。相反，尽管人们能感受到兰格对自身工具和摄影纪律的娴熟驾驭，但最让观者着迷的，依然是展览绝对私密的特质，是那种踏入私人维度的感觉——摄影不仅记录了这一维度，更助力将其揭示。《静止影像》有点像一本私密日记，我们带着些许窥阴癖的精神被邀请去其中窥探。我们看到了兰格走过的街道，看到了她在世界各地旅行时见到的人们，我们捕捉到她在面对困顿与边缘化处境时的动容，最终，我们也或多或少被一种前所未见的叙事的磁性魅力所蛊惑，而这种叙事正与她那为人熟知的公众生活并行不悖。", {"type": "paragraph", "text": "配合此次展览，读者俱乐部基金会策划了一系列名为“沿着61号公路”（Lungo la Highway 61）的讲座，与都灵王家博物馆联合举办，旨在通过摄影、音乐、历史和文学探讨美国的风景与身份。核心聚焦于乡村美国的记忆、美国梦的神话、音乐传统以及文学里的密西西比河。平行活动项目还与国家电影博物馆合作展开，放映由鲍勃·拉费尔森（Bob article_text:
Riservata e discreta, durante la presentazione della mostra Jessica Lange sceglie di cedere la parola ai rappresentanti delle istituzioni e alla curatrice, Anne Morin , e alla fine prende in mano il microfono solo quando dal pubblico le vengono personalmente rivolte delle domande. Dimentichiamo dunque la vulcanica attrice delle pellicole cinematografiche e la femme forte degli episodi di American Horror Story, per fare invece spazio ad una raffinata e timidamente elegante artista della fotografia.

Sorprende pensare che al culmine di una carriera costellata di successi, fama e red carpet nel privato Jessica Lange si sia sempre identificata come fotografa, sebbene il mondo intero la riconosca e la celebri nei panni di attrice. Una sfumatura che troviamo però perfettamente coerente con il messaggio trasmesso dalle sue opere, dove la bellezza e il fascino stanno proprio nella natura drammaticamente intima e personale di ogni scatto.

Dalla Highway 61 alla desolazione dell’America rurale. Il meglio della mostra

STILL IMAGE. Fotografie di Jessica Lange è in corso fino al 7 febbraio 2027 nelle Sale Chiablese dei Musei Reali di Torino : la rassegna si compone di oltre 200 immagini che documentano viaggi, luoghi e persone incontrati da Lange a partire dagli anni Novanta. Diverse sono le sezioni tematiche in cui il percorso è suddiviso: tra le più interessanti menzioniamo la serie Highway 61 , dedicata alla strada che da nord a sud percorre gli Stati Uniti partendo dal Minnesota, luogo di nascita dell’autrice, fino ad arrivare a New Orleans, capitale della musica jazz, e set – ricordiamolo per gli appassionati! – della terza stagione di American Horror Story, Coven . Altro interessante snodo del percorso, sempre nel solco della Lange attrice, è quello della raccolta intitolata Freak Show , i cui scatti sono stati realizzati proprio durante le riprese della serie televisiva e tra i quali non sarà affatto difficile riconoscere gli altri volti noti della saga. Le immagini proposte hanno un che di malinconico, assimilano appieno l’atmosfera angosciante della narrazione, ma paiono affondare in un tempo distante e pieno di triste turbamento.

Chiude la nostra personale classifica delle sezioni meglio riuscite del percorso la serie Presence of the Past , che riunisce diversi scatti realizzati da Lange nella pancia dell’America rurale, trapunta di luoghi segnati da catastrofi o abbandoni, crisi economiche e spopolamento, eventi che hanno gettato nell’oblio intere cittadine. Una rassegna di non-luoghi, per dirla alla Marc Augé, spazi liminali, sovente sorti intorno a grandi industrie successivamente chiuse, dove l’autrice riconosce le pallide tracce del passaggio delle persone e delle loro storie. «I gesti, le abitudini, i racconti degli uomini e delle donne che si sono stratificati in un luogo sono il motivo per cui prendo in mano la mia fotocamera e scatto» dichiara con trasporto la stessa Lange, ricordandoci che esiste un’America dimenticata e fatiscente, dove carcasse di animali imputridiscono sul ciglio della strada e dove al posto di case abitate e floride fabbriche nel pieno della produzione non è rimasto altro che il ricordo di un’umanità che un tempo vi è transitata per poi dissolversi.

Jessica Lange, le ragioni di una mostra retrospettiva

In molti saranno attratti da questa nuova rassegna innanzitutto per la popolarità dell’autrice, venerata sui social e dai tabloid come queen di stile e iconicità. Ci piace tuttavia pensare che, oltrepassata questa prima soglia, possa affiorare nella mente del pubblico un secondo livello di fruizione. È quello che si dischiude attraverso lo sguardo incantato e personale di una donna formatasi come fotografa, ma che ha poi intrapreso altre strade, e che utilizza la sua macchina Leica come medium di percezione e interpretazione del mondo, strumento di narrazione e restituzione di sensazioni e riflessioni. La bellezza di un’immagine risiede in molti aspetti: nella composizione e nel soggetto, nel taglio e nella qualità esecutiva, nella tecnica di stampa e nella costruzione prospettica.

Ebbene, Jessica Lange non presenta al pubblico fotografie universalmente impeccabili, autoriali, facilmente riconducibili a un canone o a uno standard. Al contrario, pur cogliendosi la consapevolezza con cui Lange padroneggia il proprio strumento e la disciplina fotografica, ciò che più di tutto finisce per affascinare l’osservatore è il carattere assolutamente intimo della mostra, la sensazione di varcare la soglia di una dimensione privata che la fotografia non si limita a documentare, ma contribuisce a rivelare. Still Image è un po’ come un diario intimo nel quale con spirito vagamente voyeuristico siamo invitati a sbirciare. Vediamo le strade dove la Lange ha camminato, le persone che ha visto durante i suoi viaggi in tutto il mondo, cogliamo la sua commozione davanti a situazioni di disagio e marginalità, e siamo infine un po’ stregati anche noi dal fascino magnetico di una narrazione inedita che procede in parallelo con la sua documentata vita pubblica.

Gli eventi collaterali e il public program, dal Circolo dei Lettori al Museo Nazionale del Cinema

In occasione della mostra, la Fondazione Circolo dei lettori ha curato un ciclo di incontri dal titolo Lungo la Highway 61 , organizzato con i Musei Reali di Torino per esplorare il paesaggio e l’identità degli Stati Uniti attraverso fotografia, musica, storia e letteratura. Al centro, la memoria dell’America rurale, il mito dell’American Dream, la tradizione musicale e il Mississippi letterario. Il programma degli eventi collaterali prosegue con la collaborazione del Museo Nazionale del Cinema, che propone la proiezione del film Il postino suona sempre due volte (The Postman Always Rings Twice, USA, 1981), diretto da Bob Rafelson e interpretato da Jessica Lange e Jack Nicholson. La pellicola sarà proiettata al Cinema Massimo di Torino, martedì 15 dicembre alle ore 20.30, in replica mercoledì 16 dicembre alle ore 18.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 此次袭击于2022年春天发生在乌克兰的哈尔科夫地区。

article_text:
Ukraine’s prosecutor general reported that a Russian lieutenant general has been charged in absentia for ordering a missile strike that caused significant damage to the Hryhoriy Skovoroda National Literary Memorial Museum in the country’s Kharkiv region in the spring of 2022.

As reported by The Kyiv Independent , “According to the Prosecutor General, the Russian lieutenant general who ordered the attack is originally from the village of Chuhuiv in Kharkiv Oblast and commands Russia’s 6th Guards Air and Air Defense Forces Army.”

The prosecutor general wrote, “The (lieutenant) general knew for certain that he was attacking not a military target but a monument of Ukrainian culture. Despite this, he gave the combat order to destroy it.”

The memorial museum dedicated to Skovoroda, an 18th-century philosopher steeped in the Socratic method, was housed in an estate where he lived the final years of his life and died in 1794. The institution was one of many damaged or destroyed during the siege of Ukraine. As ARTnews reported in a roundup of embattled cultural sites in the country, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, after the attack in 2022, “Last night, the Russian army deployed one of its missiles to destroy the Hryhorii Skovoroda Museum in Kharkiv Region. A missile—to destroy a museum.”

As The Kyiv Independent reported, “Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukraine’s cultural heritage since the start of the full-scale war. As of September 2026, 2,161 cultural heritage sites and 2,665 cultural institutions in Ukraine had been damaged or destroyed, according to data collected by the Culture Ministry.”
excerpt_original: The attack happened in in the country’s Kharkiv region in the spring of 2022.

article_text:
鮮やかなコラージュ技法や心温まる物語で、国境や世代を超えて親しまれてきた絵本作家エリック・カール。その作品世界に没入できるイベント「WORLD OF ERIC CARLE’S VERY IMMERSIVE EXPERIENCE（ワールド・オブ・エリック・カール ベリー・イマーシブ・エクスペリエンス）」が横浜駅直通の「アソビル」2階のイベントスペース「YOKOHAMA COAST」で、12月25日から2027年3月28日まで開催されます。

本イベントでは、『はらぺこあおむし』をはじめとするエリック・カール作品の色彩豊かな世界を、最新のデジタル技術、没入感のある空間演出、インタラクティブな体験を通じて表現。「見る・歩く・触れる・遊ぶ・つくる」といった体験を通して、まるで絵本の世界に入り込んだかのような時間を楽しむことができます。

2026年は、『はらぺこあおむし』日本語版が刊行されてから50周年を迎える記念すべき年です。この節目に開幕となる本イベントで、エリック・カール作品の新たな魅力に触れてみてはいかがでしょう。

20以上の作品に着想を得た、11の没入体験エリアを展開予定

会場内には、エリック・カールの20以上の作品に着想を得た、11の没入体験エリアを展開予定です。色彩表現やコラージュアート、自然・成長・創造性といったテーマを、映像演出や空間デザイン、参加型コンテンツによって表現。エリック・カールならではの豊かな色彩と温かみのあるテクスチャーが空間全体に広がり、来場者はまるで絵本のページの中を歩いているかのような感覚を味わうことができます。

また、会場内では作品を鑑賞するだけでなく、「歩く・触れる・遊ぶ・つくる」といった参加型コンテンツを展開。親子はもちろん、絵本ファンも楽しむことができるでしょう。

チケット

各種プレイガイド（アソビュー！・セブンチケット・イープラス・ZAIKO）にてチケットが販売されています。一般チケットに加え、親子で楽しめる「親子ペアチケット」も。詳細は 公式ホームページ をご覧ください。

article_text:
Jason Statham ‘s retired “Beekeeper” Adam Clay is back to take on his makers in the sequel to his 2024 action pic.

On Thursday, Amazon MGM Studios released the first teaser for the Timo Tjahjanto-helmed sequel The Beekeeper 2 , which premieres in theaters on Jan. 15, 2027 and sees Statham reprise his role as the former assassin.

In The Beekeeper 2 , Clay is a wanted man pulled back into the fight when the Beekeeper organization goes rogue and sets its sights on controlling the government. In order to clear his name, Clay must save the president of the United States and take on the very group that made him.

Related Stories

Amazon MGM Studios & Miramax’s ‘The Beekeeper 2’ To Buzz Into Theaters Next Winter

Amazon MGM Lands Worldwide Rights To Jason Statham Sequel ‘Beekeeper 2’ In $50M+ Deal

The sneak peek features Statham kicking butt to Metallica’s “For Whom the Bell Tolls” before landing a classic Statham zinger.

Watch on Deadline

Penned by Kurt Wimmer and Zak Penn, the sequel also stars Pom Klementieff, Jemma Redgrave, Emmy Raver-Lampman, Adam Copeland, Bobby Naderi, Yara Shahidi and Jeremy Irons.

Producers include Statham, Chris Long, p.g.a. and Kurt Wimmer, with executive producers Jonathan Glickman, Thom Zadra, Alexandra Loewy, Rachael Cole and David Ayer, as well as co-producers Anthony M. Scott, Spencer Ela and Asa Sims.

article_text:
Stories Unfold

Paintings by Ndikhumbule Ngqinambi (SA) & Ethnographic Objects from New Guinea

Galerie Lemaire is pleased to present the exhibition Stories Unfold , featuring works by South African artist Ndikhumbule Ngqinambi (Cape Town, 1977) alongside ethnographic objects from New Guinea. This dialogue between contemporary painting and traditional artifacts invites reflection on the power of image and narrative, and how these can be expressed across cultures through diverse techniques and materials.

Ngqinambi is a self-taught artist whose figurative paintings are layered with meaning. His narratives are ambiguous, while his style is layered. He draws inspiration from music, film, dance, and theatre.

The works on view at Galerie Lemaire include titles such as The Watchers, A Film Not Made Yet, and Unfinished Stories. They portray figures in motion, captured in cinematic moments between past and future. Themes of time, transition, and dreamlike states are central in his work. By contrast, the ethnographic objects from New Guinea—statues, masks, and ritual artefacts—do not immediately reveal their stories to the uninformed viewer. Their meanings unfold only for those familiar with their cultural context. Yet, they share a common potential with Ngqinambi’s paintings: opening a window onto another world, another way of seeing.

Stories Unfold demonstrates how imagery—whether in paintings or ritual objects—can convey narratives that are at times recognizable, at times mysterious, but always meaningful.

Exhibition Details

Opening Reception: December 13, 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM Dates: 13 December 2025 – 31 January 2026 Venue: Galerie Lemaire Reguliersgracht 80 1017 LV Amsterdam www.gallery-lemaire.com Opening Hours: Thursday, Friday, Saturday, 11:00 AM – 5:00 PM This exhibition has been organized in collaboration with SBK Amsterdam and Fons Geerlings (Galerie 23).

article_text:
H artlepool fisherman Stan Rennie has been called the next Mr Bates . For nearly 50 years Rennie has fished the same stretch of northeast coastline – then in October 2021, thousands of crabs, starfish and lobsters washed up dead and dying on the beaches. “It was like something out of a horror film,” says one local. Rennie and other fishermen suspected industrial pollution, but an investigation by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs concluded that the most likely cause of the die-off was “algal bloom”. For Rennie and the other fisherman, it didn’t add up. So, they crowdfunded their own independent scientific study.

This documentary from Jeanie Finlay ( Your Fat Friend ) tells the story, and it’s maddening. The fishermen are close to bankruptcy, they’ve got mortgages and kids, catches are down 80%. The cost of diesel is higher than the price of a haul, and most put their boats up for sale. “Any jobs in Lidl?” reads one placard as they protest through town. What the fishermen suspect is that toxic sediment dredged from the River Tees and dumped in the sea is to blame. Their investigation finds evidence of a link to the chemical pyridine , a byproduct of steelmaking.

The reason for the dredging is the development of the then Conservative government’s flagship freeport (a zone with tax and customs breaks to attract investment) in the Tees Valley. The freeport was seen as key to the Tories’ “levelling-up” agenda after Brexit – and there’s footage of Boris Johnson at the site in his favourite dressing-up costume, a hi-vis vest. The gaslighting of fishermen and their concerns by public officials is enraging. Tees Valley mayor Ben Houchen brushes them off as conspiracy theorists, crackpots and – a word he delivers with a sneer – activists. But, like Alan Bates, Rennie refuses to give up. “If an activist is someone who is trying to stop the ecosystem being killed, I’m an activist.”

article_text:
When KJ Apa was being considered to star as Jimmy Stewart in the new biopic “Jimmy,” he took another look at “It’s a Wonderful Life.”

“I was watching and thinking, how am I going to pull this off?” the actor, who is best known for his starring role as Archie in the CW coming-of-age series “Riverdale,” tells me. “I don’t look anything like him. I don’t sound anything like him. I’m not as tall as him. Like none of it lined up, but by the end of the movie, I was like, ‘I have to do it.’”

Related Stories

“Jimmy,” directed by Aaron Burns, chronicles Stewart’s rise in Hollywood and time fighting in WWII. After winning an Oscar for “The Philadelphia Story” in 1941, he was drafted to serve in the war. Rather than use his celebrity clout to dodge the draft, Stewart enlisted and flew 20 missions over Europe and rose to the rank of colonel.

Popular on Variety

When he returned home from the war, however, Hollywood seemed to have forgotten about him. Stewart considered moving back home to Indiana, Pennsylvania to work in his father’s general store. But Frank Capra convinced him to star as George Bailey in what is now considered one of the greatest films of all time, the 1946 Christmas classic “It’s a Wonderful Life.”

“Frank Capra gave him that script and he was going through a lot of what George Bailey was going through,” said Apa, who will receive a Spotlight Award on Oct. 18 at the Newport Beach Film Festival. “I honestly think ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ was like therapy for him. He was able to continue in his career. His daughter Kelly told me when he came back from the war, he said he wasn’t sure if he was a retired actor or a retired pilot. He just didn’t know what he was doing. I think he was lost.”

I sat down with Apa before the recent world premiere of “Jimmy” at the Heartland Film Festival in Indianapolis. We talked about finding Stewart’s voice, being open about his addictions and recovery and speculation that he is the singer Mr. Fantasy.

Quick note: I make a brief cameo in the film as bandleader Glenn Miller.

What did you know about Jimmy Stewart before signing on for the movie?

Growing up in New Zealand, I didn’t know much about old Hollywood. I wasn’t familiar with the old Hollywood movie stars.

Take me through the process of getting Jimmy Stewart’s voice?

I was meant to shoot a movie called “The Sublime Biopic” about the band Sublime. [Apa was set to star as the band’s late frontman Bradley Nowell]. I was working with a dialect coach, Eliza Simpson, at the time and she’s phenomenal. I worked with her every second of every day for “Jimmy.” I watched all his films. I would listen to him over and over and over again. You just have to spend a lot of time listening and repeating, listening and repeating, listening and repeating.

His voice is so specific and iconic. It’s not like you could practice by using it when you’re at Starbucks.

For “Sublime,” I would do that. I’d go out and I’d talk to people in the accent. No one would think that wasn’t my voice. You’re totally right with this one. I was in no man’s land for the duration of the prep. I had not shared it with anyone. I was terrified. My only sounding board was Eliza.

What was it like shooting your first scene using Jimmy’s voice?

It was really nerve-wracking. It could go two ways. I realized it was such a fine line.

You didn’t want to sound like an “SNL” skit.

Exactly, which, by the way, I did read some of the things online. They were pretty funny. But at the end of the day, it’s completely out of my control. I can only focus on what I’m doing with the actors that I’m working with and with Aaron. There’s only so much that I can control. If I look like a fool, I look like a fool. I did my best.

What do you want people to learn about Jimmy Stewart from the movie?

I want people to have the same feeling I had when I first read the script, which was it was unimaginable for me to believe that he was such a highly decorated actor, and then served for over 20 years as a B-24 bomber pilot. He was involved with the D-Day invasion and then came back and did like 50-plus movies. Frank Capra gave him that script and he was going through a lot of what George Bailey was going through. I honestly think “It’s a Wonderful Life” was like therapy for him. He was able to continue in his career. His daughter Kelly told me when he came back from the war, he said he wasn’t sure if he was a retired actor or a retired pilot. He just didn’t know what he was doing. I think he was lost. But I want people to know what he did for this country.

Has Mr. Fantasy seen the film?

I have to ask him, but I think Mr. Fantasy would love this movie because he is such a positive guy and it’s a movie that will make you feel good. It’s not political. It’s not controversial. It’s about a man who doesn’t do the easy thing. He does the thing that he feels is the right thing to do, which is to serve his country because his father did the same, and his father’s father did the same.

What do you say when people ask you if you’re Mr. Fantasy?

I say the truth, which is no. Listen, I wish that I could have the confidence to do what that guy does. I mean, he’s just so himself. The energy that guy has!

This summer on Dylan Sprouse’s podcast “Wildmen,” you talked about your struggles with food. You’ve also been open about your addiction and recovery. Do you ever worry that you’re putting yourself out there too much?

It really doesn’t get more simple than that I’m a good friend of Dylan Sprouse. He asked me to come on his podcast. I had just dropped my son back off to his mum’s house. I was completely unprepared. I just rolled up and sat down, and we started talking, and I felt in that moment like, this is who I am. This is a huge part of who I am. These thoughts that go into an eating disorder or drug addiction or other addictions, they are all part of who I am and have taken up so much of my life. I’ve had so many people come up to me saying, “Thanks for sharing that.” I honestly didn’t realize that it would have that reaction. It was cool.

“Jimmy” is in theaters on Nov. 6.

article_text:
News

Christine Sun Kim Awarded 2026 MacArthur Fellowship

CHRISTINE SUN KIM . Courtesy the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

The MacArthur Foundation has named mixed-media artist Christine Sun Kim as one of its 2026 MacArthur Fellows. She is one of 20 recipients, among them the artists Rodney McMillian, Chip Thomas, and Vincent Valdez. Each fellow will be granted a sum of USD 800,000 over the course of five years to facilitate their research and practice.

Born in California in 1980 and based in Berlin, Kim has been Deaf since birth. Initially wanting to pursue graphic design but told that no university courses offered interpreters, she instead completed a BFA at the School of Visual Arts in New York in 2006, followed by an MFA in sound and music at Bard College in 2013. In her early career, she began to draw on her own experience as a Deaf person to explore how communication is navigated throughout cultures. In 2019 she participated in the Whitney Biennial with her Degrees of Deaf Rage series (2018–19), which comprises charcoal illustrations expressing her frustration at the hurdles she had faced in cultural institutions. In 2020, she received the Ford Foundation’s Disability Future Fellowship.

Her practice has since expanded into performance, music, and interactive installation, using dry humor to raise awareness of Deaf issues and to probe the societal, cultural, and bodily relationships to language and sound. Kim’s work has been exhibited internationally, including at the Museum of Modern Art, New York (2013); the Shanghai and Berlin Biennales (both 2016); the Museum für Moderne Kunst, Frankfurt (2021); the Secession in Vienna (2023); the Gwangju Biennale (2023); and the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea, Seoul (2026).

The MacArthur Fellowship, informally known as the “genius grant,” has been awarded annually since 1981 to people in fields ranging from writing and the arts to science and teaching. Kristen Mack, vice president of communications for MacArthur Fellows and Partnerships, stated that past fellows have “defied boundaries by questioning conventions, crossing disciplines, and driving collective progress.” The foundation described Kim as an artist befitting of this legacy, citing her ability to explore “the political, cultural, and multisensory dimensions of sound, spoken language, and communication.”

Harison Butler is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.
excerpt_original: The artist is among 20 recipients of the coveted “genius grant.” Harison Butler

article_text:
ミュージアムパーク茨城県自然博物館（茨城県坂東市）で、第96回企画展「日本列島誕生のひみつ～石から発見！ 大地の成り立ち～」が2027年2月7日（日）まで開催されています。

私たちが住んでいる日本列島は、数千万年前には今のような姿ではなかったと考えられています。では、どのように日本列島は誕生したのでしょうか？ 本企画展では、全国のさまざまな石から、日本列島の大地の成り立ちが紹介されます。

第96回企画展「日本列島誕生のひみつ～石から発見！ 大地の成り立ち～」

会場：ミュージアムパーク茨城県自然博物館（茨城県坂東市大崎700）

会期：2026年10月24日（土）～2027年2月7日（日）

開館時間：9:30～17:00（入館は16:30まで）

休館日：月曜日（月曜日が祝日の場合はその翌日以降）、年末年始（12/28～1/1）

入館料（企画展開催期）： 一般850円、高校生520円、小・中学生170円、満70歳以上420円 ※未就学児は無料

アクセス： 東武野田線愛宕駅から茨城急行バス「岩井車庫」行きで約15分、「自然博物館入口」下車徒歩10分。つくばエクスプレス・関東鉄道守谷駅から関東鉄道バス「岩井バスターミナル」行きで約30分、「自然博物館入口」下車徒歩10分。常磐自動車道谷和原ICから車で約20分

詳細は、 ミュージアムパーク茨城県自然博物館公式サイト まで。

展示の見どころ

展示は「第1章 大地は動いている」「第2章 日本列島誕生を知るカギ」「第3章 日本列島をつくる石はどこからきた」「第4章 大陸がさけてできた日本列島」「第5章 変わり続ける日本列島」「第6章 日本列島をつくる石を見に行こう！」からなる全6章構成。日本各地のさまざまな石や地層、化石から、日本列島の大地の成り立ちに焦点が当てられます。

見どころ１：「日本列島の成り立ち紹介」

日本列島の土台ができた時代から現代まで47都道府県の石から紹介されます。

見どころ２：「日本列島誕生のひみつを見に行きたくなる！」

たくさんの現地の写真が展示されるとともに、県の石やジオパークも紹介されます。

見どころ３：「地質が好きになる」

展示室では、貴重な標本だけでなく、映像展示やハンズオン展示なども豊富に用意されます。様々な切り口で地質に触れることで、より深く興味が持てるはずです。

足元に転がる石や旅先で出会う雄大な岩壁には、遥かなる地球の営みと列島形成の記憶が刻まれています。本展は、北は北海道から南は沖縄まで全国47都道府県の石を通して、私たちが暮らす大地の壮大な成り立ちを五感で体感できる貴重な機会です。現地の美しい景観写真やジオパークの解説に触れれば、きっとその土地を実際に訪れてみたくなるはず。さらに、見て触れて動かせるハンズオン展示や映像も充実しており、大人から子どもまで楽しみながら地質の世界に引き込まれていくことでしょう。悠久の時が織りなす大地のドラマを確かめに、ぜひ本展に足を運んでみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
SPOILER ALERT: This story reveals major details about Peter Berg’s new real-life World War II film “ The Mosquito Bowl .”

When British actor Tom Francis signed with his U.S. agents at CAA, he made his aspirations very clear.

“One of the first emails I sent to my agents was, ‘This is a list of directors who I want to work with and why,’” Francis tells me. “Pete was right at the top of the list because I love ‘Friday Night Lights.’”

Related Stories

‘Pride and Prejudice’ Trailer: Emma Corrin and Jack Lowden Reboot Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy's Love Story for Netflix

AI Can Cut Film Budgets by Up to 40%, Says ‘The Outlaws’ Director Kang Yoon-sung, as Netflix Reveals Use on 300 Titles: ‘A Human Touch Is Absolutely Essential’

Pete is Peter Berg.

Francis can check Berg off that list because he co-stars in the director’s latest movie, “The Mosquito Bowl,” which tells the true story of four college football stars who were served in the Marines during World War II.

Francis plays David Schreiner alongside Nicholas Galitzine as John McLaughry, Ray Nicholson as Tony Butkovich and Bill Skarsgård as Bob Baumann.

“I remember getting the call and to be able to work with Pete, the way his mind works, the way he views the word, I think is incredible,” Francis says. “He’s helped me through some really tough times. He’s very, very open and warm and honest and loving. He welcomes you into a family, and he’ll be there for you whenever you need him.”

Francis comes to the big screen via the West End and Broadway. In “Sunset Boulevard,” he won a Laurence Olivier Award and earned a Tony nomination for his Broadway debut opposite Nicole Scherzinger in Jamie Lloyd’s “Sunset Boulevard.” His previous stage work includes “Rent,” “& Juliet” and “Hair.” He made his movie debut in Noah Baumbach’s “Jay Kelly” and appeared in the fifth and final season of the Netflix series “You.”

While Schreiner wasn’t a singer in real life, Berg decided to show off Francis’ vocal chops in “The Mosquito Bowl,” adding a scene at the last minute that features Francis singing in a bar before the men are shipped off to war. “Pete sent me the song and he was like, ‘Just learn this for tomorrow’ and I was like, ‘OK, cool,’” Francis remembers. “I had no idea what I was going to be doing with it. I thought it was going to be around a campfire. I didn’t realize it was going to be fully staged.”

“The Mosquito Bowl” is brutal in its graphic depiction of the battlefield. It is heartbreaking in that McLaughry is the only one of the four men who survived the war. The film is based on Buzz Bissinger’s book “The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II,” about the Mosquito Bowl football game that the Marines played while preparing for the Battle of Okinawa. Retired Marine Corps Sgt.

“I remember Jacques [Jouffret, the cinematographer] said to me, ‘Listen, Tom, the thing I don’t want to do it romanticize this,’” Francis says. “He was like, ‘We bought loads and loads of palm trees, but I’m not shooting the palm trees. We’re setting them on fire. We can’t glorify this. It has to be as true to what they went through as possible.’ Obviously, what we did there is no comparison in any way, shape, or form, but in visual terms, trying to replicate it in a visual tone, I think Jacques and Pete did a really visceral and intense job. It’s uncomfortable at points.”

The end credits list the men’s age, all of whom were just 24 during WWII.

“They were so young. They had so much life to live. They had families they left. They had future families to make,” Francis says. “They had friends they left, future friends that they left. They had jobs, promotions, just everything. I have so much respect for that generation and every generation that’s come before them and after them.”

Francis also talked about returning to theater. “I really miss the adrenaline,” he says. “I really want to do a play. I want to do something original. I’ve done a lot of revivals or stepped into things, and especially with this movie, doing something for the first time, you have so much ownership over it. There’s responsibility of just like making sure that you can tell the story that you really want to want to tell. I think there’s something really exciting about that.”

Francis adds with a smile, “I really love being in movies.”

“The Misquito Bowl” is in theaters now. It debuts on Netflix Nov. 25.
